6.name: Felix and Sable ride forest road
6.description: Felix and Sable travel quickly together along a dirt road through the forest.
evidence: Felix and Sable ride a dirt road through tall pines, moving at pace.
Sable rides beside Felix, her long dark brown hair pulled back under a riding hood.

6.name: Felix predicts Wren's smuggling route
6.description: Felix states that if Wren has the map, he will move it through the eastern fences as he has done before.
evidence:
FELIX
If Wren has the map he will move it through the eastern fences. He has done it before.

6.name: Felix identifies Wren as powerful nobleman
6.description: Felix explains his certainty by revealing that Wren is a nobleman with influence across three provinces.
evidence:
SABLE
How can you be certain?

FELIX
Because of who he is. A nobleman with reach across three provinces.

6.name: Felix says thief described wrong map
6.description: Felix explains that the thief's description matched a convincing but incorrect version of the map.
evidence:
SABLE
What about the description the thief gave? You said it was wrong.

FELIX
They described a map of the Northern Reaches drawn in red ink on reinforced parchment. That matches the work closely -- closely enough that someone who had seen it briefly or heard it described secondhand might believe it.

6.name: Felix cites Holt's fence report
6.description: Felix confirms that the red-ink description came from how Holt said the fence described the map.
evidence:
FELIX
That is how Holt said the fence described it.

6.name: Felix explains thieves searched old hiding place
6.description: Felix says the thieves must have previously seen the map in his wooden box on the window alcove shelf and assumed it was still there.
evidence:
SABLE
And the chest -- where they found it. The window alcove?

FELIX
They must have seen it earlier in the wooden box I kept on the alcove shelf. They assumed it was still there when they came back for it.

6.name: Felix reveals he moved the map
6.description: Felix states that the map was no longer in the alcove because he had moved it, though not soon enough to prevent the larger problem.
evidence:
FELIX
No. I had moved it. Too late, as it turns out.
